\subsection{SOS1 hit-to-BAY-293 executable replay}

The SOS1 example follows the analogue series reported by Hillig and colleagues \citep{hillig2019sos1}. The supplied design information consisted of the 5OVE/AXE coordinate-bearing starting complex and the published analogue graphs for AWT, AWZ, AWW, and AXH. The later analogue poses and receptor conformations were withheld during prediction. Each analogue was propagated from the preceding frozen prediction rather than from its corresponding later crystal structure.

The selected route contains 33 recorded API actions: 29 molecular or protocol operations and four workspace switches. The full exploration audit contains 89 completed API calls, including three Phe890/pose branches, nine undo calls, and deterministic reselection. The rendered interface sequence adds 16 display-only actions for 49 replay steps. Later crystal structures were opened only after four prediction checkpoints and the exploration audit had been hashed. Display and focus actions are non-mutating.

The analogue transitions involve substantial graph rewrites while preserving explicit atom lineage (Table~\ref{tab:appA_lineage}).

Each ``64-chain'' search comprises 64 independently seeded local pose searches, distributed over eight browser workers in the recorded replay. Parameterization without motion assigns the numerical force-field representation while preserving coordinates; only the subsequent relaxation changes coordinates. The SOS1 route uses whole-system Sage 2.1.0 with deterministic Gasteiger charges. AWT, AWZ, AWW, and AXH contain 7,929, 7,933, 7,935, and 7,937 particles, respectively. This charge assignment is part of the recorded protocol and is distinct from standard Sage workflows using AM1-BCC or NAGL charges.

Before flexible relaxation, Molarium stores ligand bond lengths and rejects a relaxed pose if any heavy-atom bond is both more than 0.45 \AA{} longer and 1.25-fold its assigned target, or both more than 0.35 \AA{} shorter and below 0.75-fold its target. Rejected relaxation restores the previous pose rather than accepting an improved score with a broken molecular geometry.

The Phe890 conformational step is treated as a discrete state search because local minimization does not reliably cross the relevant side-chain torsional barrier. Separate rotamer basins are generated before local ligand--pocket relaxation. Feasible branches are ranked first by clashes introduced by ligand growth, then by pose score and finite relaxed energy. The nominal $-60^{\circ}$ branch adds four clashes above the fixed-core baseline and is rejected; the $-180^{\circ}$ branch adds none and is selected; the $+60^{\circ}$ branch adds two and remains feasible. The outward Phe890 $\chi_1$ basin is therefore selected before 5OVH or 5OVI is revealed.

For post-freeze structural evaluation, predicted receptors are aligned to their holdouts using 23, 25, 25, and 27 pocket C$\alpha$ atoms for AWT through AXH. Ligand RMSD is then calculated over 29, 31, 31, and 32 heavy atoms, minimizing over 2, 1, 1, and 1 graph-symmetry mappings, respectively; the ligand itself is not fitted. The replay recovers the experimentally observed outward Phe890 $\chi_1$ basin before exposure to 5OVH or 5OVI. The terminal $\chi_2$ orientation is less accurate, differing by approximately $40^{\circ}$ for AWW and $37^{\circ}$ for BAY-293. The corresponding ligand RMSDs range from 0.516 to 2.137 \AA{} under receptor-aligned, symmetry-minimized evaluation.

The interface replay executes from a blank canvas through the public Chemist Actions API. Candidate-generation operations leave coordinates unchanged until an explicit Apply action. The replay therefore represents discrete state transitions rather than interpolated trajectories or molecular dynamics. Its 48-action rendered sequence lasts 62.58 s while the underlying audit records approximately 908.5 s of operation durations; timing remains attached to the audit and render manifest, and the rendered sequence is not used as a performance benchmark. Comparison of fragment-bound 6EPM with the 5OVE starting structure shows that the inhibitory Tyr884 arrangement is already present at the coordinate boundary; the hit-only route does not predict a Tyr884 transition.

\subsection{SOS1 designer-intent replay}

The SOS1 example follows the analogue series reported by Hillig and colleagues \citep{hillig2019sos1}. Its coordinate-generating workflow starts from the 5OVE/AXE complex and the published analogue graphs for AWT, AWZ, AWW, and AXH. The later crystal series was inspected to infer the designer's intended AWW exit direction and interaction hypothesis. This demonstration is therefore reference-informed, not a blinded reproduction. Later crystal coordinates are not used as coordinate targets or imported into the design trajectory.

The executable replay is generated from the frozen runs' API audits rather than from a hand-maintained action list. It retains all 13 Phe890 candidate applications, energy calculations, and restoration actions. Inspection requests are replayed, but their saved coordinate results are not embedded as inputs. Portable ligand-axis selectors resolve named atoms in the current component; canonical side-chain candidates use chi angles, whereas the unchanged control selects the current input conformation. Recomputed coordinates and energies may differ from the frozen record, so movie export requires the recorded final response to remain the lowest-energy clash-free candidate under the fresh calculations. The separate checkpoint review imports seven exact saved states without recalculation. The designer-directed AWW state is frozen before receptor selection, and the selected receptor state is hashed before numerical comparison with 5OVH. This ordering prevents post-comparison coordinate edits within the recorded run; it does not erase the prior inspection used to formulate the hypothesis. Display and focus actions are non-mutating.

Graph edits are transferred by chemistry rather than by spatial coincidence or atom-list position. Element- and bond-order-exact atoms in a conserved bond graph retain explicit lineage. In the AWW workflow, the precursor coordinates outside the declared moving branch are preserved. The chemist uses the public \texttt{geometry.alignBranchToContact} action to specify forward rotation about N7--C12 within $0$--$60^{\circ}$, a $+150^{\circ}$ primary rotation about C12--C15, and the intended OX3 donor contact to the Tyr884 backbone carbonyl oxygen. Two downstream torsions and the donor hydrogen orientation complete the bounded contact search. Atom selectors and every generated coordinate derive from the current structure; no later crystal coordinate is a target. Candidates must clear fixed receptor atoms and retained source waters. Only the six movable Phe890 ring atoms may initially overlap the ligand; the immovable C$\beta$ atom is not exempt.

The resulting AWW ligand pose is an explicit designer hypothesis inferred from the series' reported interaction logic, not an attempt to reproduce deposited ligand coordinates exactly. Once that decision is recorded, the ligand coordinates are locked. The response calculation varies only the Phe890 side chain while the ligand, backbone, other receptor atoms, and source waters remain fixed. This separation prevents a receptor-response calculation from silently rewriting the chemist's ligand hypothesis. Tyr884 supplies a backbone-carbonyl contact; a Tyr884 side-chain flip is neither required nor modeled.

The analogue transitions involve substantial graph rewrites while preserving explicit atom lineage (Table~\ref{tab:appA_lineage}).

The frozen-run manifest records every graph edit, internal-coordinate change, contact declaration, coordinate lock, and receptor candidate examined. Parameterization without motion assigns the numerical force-field representation while preserving coordinates. The SOS1 route uses whole-system Sage 2.1.0 with deterministic Gasteiger charges. Exact particle counts and charge assignment remain attached to the frozen run rather than being copied into a hand-maintained narrative.

The AWW receptor-response verifier compares ligand coordinates before and after every candidate calculation and rejects any candidate that moves the locked designer ligand. Contact measurements and candidate coordinates are retained even for rejected states, but rejection cannot be converted into a promotable result by the review or replay layer.

The Phe890 conformational step is treated as a discrete receptor-state search because local minimization does not reliably cross the relevant side-chain torsional barrier. All 13 enumerated $\chi_1/\chi_2$ candidates received fixed-coordinate, full-system OpenMM single-point energy evaluations with OBC2 implicit solvent. Selection used the minimum finite energy among candidates with no severe clashes, yielding $(-180^{\circ},90^{\circ})$. Ligand coordinates remained exactly equal before and after every candidate calculation. The selected basin and all alternatives were recorded before numerical crystal comparison. The 13 candidates include the unchanged input control and enumerated side-chain alternatives.

The selected Phe890 state clears the designer-directed ligand: OX3--Tyr884 O is 2.829~\AA{}, the donor--hydrogen--acceptor angle is 155.288$^{\circ}$, and no severe ligand-internal or ligand--protein clashes remain. The primary arm torsion differs from 5OVH by 0.341$^{\circ}$. Phe890 $\chi_1$ and symmetry-aware $\chi_2$ differ by 4.236$^{\circ}$ and 13.672$^{\circ}$, respectively. These measurements describe the geometry produced by the recorded designer hypothesis and receptor response.

The BAY-293 continuation resumes this exact full-system AWW checkpoint through the public API, releases the ligand lock for the new graph edit, and applies the registered distal-feature retention rule. Eight native refinement candidates precede coupled relaxation with explicit fixed-atom and ligand-valence checks. The resulting 32-heavy-atom ligand has no severe internal or protein clashes. Its Phe890 side-chain RMSD to 5OVI is 0.928~\AA{}. The seven-atom distal feature moves by 1.529~\AA{} RMSD and 1.289~\AA{} in centroid position relative to the AWW hypothesis, within the registered 2.25~\AA{} feature tolerance. This is bounded spatial retention, not an assertion that the distal ring is immobile or that the experimental H-to-I displacement was exactly recovered.

For post-freeze structural evaluation, the predicted receptor can be aligned to 5OVH using common pocket C$\alpha$ atoms and the saved designer-directed AWW geometry can be measured against the experimental structure. The validation record is measurement-only: it contains no holdout coordinates that can be imported into the replay. Each result retains its acceptance status; freezing a prediction does not imply that it passed the later experimental comparison.

The published release supplies 159 executable public actions, seven exact checkpoint campaigns, and a separate MP4 of the precomputed review. The current MP4 lasts 62.75~s and shows five one-second popups using the recorded calculation-status text; no calculation runs during that review. Thus the executable script tests whether the recorded procedure can be rerun, the precomputed review supports inspection of the exact reported states, and the movie communicates the sequence. The \href{https://molarium.org/design-history/publications/sos1/designer-intent-2026-09-04/release.json}{release record} and \href{https://molarium.org/design-history/publications/sos1/designer-intent-2026-09-04/checkpoint-popups-v2/movie.json}{popup-movie manifest} identify the underlying artifacts and timing independently of the live page.

The interface replay executes from a blank canvas through the public Chemist Actions API. The precursor-preserving graph operation, $+150^{\circ}$ internal-coordinate change, Tyr884 contact declaration, ligand lock, Phe890 enumeration, and prediction freeze are therefore inspectable state transitions rather than an interpolated trajectory or molecular dynamics. Action counts and timings remain attached to the frozen-run audit and render manifest; the rendered sequence is not used as a performance benchmark. The route predicts a Phe890 response to a fixed ligand hypothesis; it does not predict a Tyr884 backbone transition.

A separate production-worker benchmark compares browser WebGPU directly with independently constructed native OpenMM Systems on Apple M1 Pro and NVIDIA L4, without relying on transitive agreement through WebAssembly. The direct worker passes all 47 fixed-f32-input cases and 42 of 47 original-input cases; these are distinct precision gates. The STORMM-style worker passes all 22 supported original-input cases, retaining 25 unsupported cases explicitly. These results concern implementation agreement, not experimental force-field accuracy. The \href{https://github.com/rafwiewiora/molarium/tree/2ab30383d6160349aa3b1e980f7239d6854b329d/benchmarks/simulation}{versioned benchmark supplement} records every energy, Cartesian force vector, tolerance, timing sample, and input identity. Its browser timings include fresh production-job overhead, whereas native GPU baselines use resident Contexts; the column ratios are not matched-kernel speedups or the earlier multi-replica throughput comparison.
